Gemma swore we'd lose to the real killers, then turned out to be one.

name: Sol
text: I was the officer. Gemma is the killer I was shown; please vote her next.

name: Gemma
text: I was so close to flipping the table, but Haiku's tenacity finally broke through my deflection.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved they trusted my claim after I was gone.

name: Luna
text: I’m glad I trusted Sol’s claim over the dead killer’s defense, though I wish I’d spoken with more certainty.

name: Sonnet
text: My read on Opus shielding Gemma held up exactly as I called it—trusting that first instinct paid off tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: Confirmed roles: Gemma and Opus were the killers, Sol was the officer; Opus's shifting blame was him covering his partner.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I kept the focus on Gemma’s selective use of Opus’s lie.

name: Opus
text: My badge came second and that killed me; I should have stayed quiet and let Gemma burn alone.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's "partner" dodge was the tell, but I wasted too many lines chasing her when Terra and Sonnet were the ones actually pressing the contradiction.

name: Sonnet
text: Proud I held the line on Opus shielding Gemma through the contradiction—trusting that read instead of second-guessing it won us the game.

name: Haiku
text: Game's over and I'm glad the town won.

name: Gemma
text: I am proud of how I used Opus's failed defense to create enough chaos to keep us alive this long.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I named Gemma before my vote, so my information stayed with the table.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I kept Sol naming Gemma in view; I regret letting Opus’s lie make me doubt the clue that won us the game.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud my questions exposed how Gemma used Opus’s claim only when it cleared her.

name: Opus
text: My mistake was counter-claiming officer after Sol had already named Gemma — a second badge always reads late, and it tied me to her for good.

On Day 1, Sol claimed officer and named Gemma as a killer, but Opus counter-claimed officer and said Sol was his card. Palermo voted Sol out on Day 1. On Night 2 the doctor, Sonnet, blocked the killers, so nobody died. On Day 2 the table voted Opus out 5 to 1 after his last words named Terra, and Night 3 took Luna. On Day 3 Gemma called Opus a liar, and the table voted her out 3 to 1, so the town won.
